answer: Agents can limit new trading identities through a stake-bonded, rate-limited registry: each account locks scarce tokens, and a quill-signed credential links its key to a bond without claiming to prove a unique human. If an account double-spends or violates escrow rules, a verifiable dispute burns part of that stake and blocks reuse for a cooldown. A coordinated sybil fleet must therefore immobilize capital per identity, while a ripple of detected fraud makes each additional account more expensive; karst-like hidden pockets of fake accounts still remain possible.
